title: Planetary Science and Astronomy, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: University Park. Needed three new department catalogs (EARTH, GEOG, METEO) beyond the ASTRO/GEOSC catalogs already scraped for Astronomy and Astrophysics. 'etm' marks the gateway courses (Calc I, ASTRO 1) everything downstream depends on. Post-parens-fix re-scrape (AND/OR prereq-parsing bug fix) revealed CHEM 110's real prereq is MATH 22 (previously empty) -- MATH 140/141 (this plan's own Calc I/II track) do NOT substitute for it -- and MATH 22 itself real-chains through MATH 21, MATH 4, and MATH 3, none of which were in the plan. With CHEM 110 permanently stuck, CHEM 111/112/113 and GEOSC 474/BIOL 474 (both need CHEM 110 directly) were also unschedulable; STAT 200 (needs MATH 21 directly) was blocked the same way. Added the real chain explicitly: MATH 3 (Semester 1), MATH 4 (Semester 2), MATH 21 (Semester 3), MATH 22 (Semester 4) -- same convention used for LSCPE/ABSM/MATSCI's identical gap. 2026-08-27 verification against the live bulletin's own program-requirements text found and fixed real gaps: (1) the 'select one of ASTRO 1/5/6/291' and 'select one of GEOSC 1/EARTH 2/GEOSC 20' picks were each hardcoded to a single course with no alternatives -- widened to the bulletin's real full option lists. (2) the intro-programming pick only offered CMPSC 121/201, missing the bulletin's own CMPSC 101/203 (CMPSC 202 appears in the bulletin's table with a blank title and doesn't exist in the scraped catalog, so it's treated as a rendering artifact and excluded). (3) The real 'select three of ASTRO 120/130/140/292' (9 credits) requirement was double-modeled -- two hardcoded required items plus three more generic 'Advanced Elective' slots drew from the same 4-course pool, totaling 18 credits against a real 9 and structurally unfillable (only 1 of the 3 extra slots could ever find an unused course). Replaced with exactly 3 shared-option-pool items that de-duplicate naturally (see each item's own notes). (4) The real 'select 12 credits' EARTH/GEOSC/METEO list was modeled as 4 single-option hardcoded items -- widened all 4 to share the real full list so any valid combination is recognized. (5) 'Supporting Courses: Select 11 credits ... from department list' was modeled as 3 slots totaling only 9 credits -- bumped to 11 (one slot raised to 5cr) and wired via open_elective, same convention as MICRB Elective List C's identical shortfall. Net effect of these fixes was a 9-credit reduction (removing the double-modeled Advanced Elective slots) more than offsetting the 2-credit Supporting Course increase, so this still fits within the existing 17cr/semester cap without needing a bump.

items.label: MATH 3 (unlocks MATH 4, needed for CHEM 110's real MATH 22 prereq chain -- MATH 140/141 don't substitute)
Advanced Elective (ASTRO 120/130/140/292) -- pick 1 of 3
items.notes: Wired 2026-08-27 per the live bulletin's real 'Select three of the following: ASTRO 120/130/140/292' (9 credits) requirement (planetary-science-and-astronomy-bs_programrequirementstext.pdf). Previously this pool was double-modeled: two hardcoded 'required' items forced ASTRO 120 AND ASTRO 130 AND ASTRO 140 specifically (via an 'or, distinct from the earlier pick' hack), and three MORE generic 'Advanced Elective' slots were added on top drawing from the same 4-course pool -- mathematically impossible to fill (at most 1 of the 3 extra slots could ever find an unused course, ASTRO 292) and 18 credits modeled against a real 9-credit requirement. Replaced with exactly 3 shared-option-pool course items (same de-duplication mechanism already used elsewhere for shared pools like CAS 100A/B/C), letting the engine naturally resolve them to 3 distinct real courses.

items.label: Supporting Course
items.notes: Wired 2026-08-27. The bulletin names no specific course list beyond 'department list' -- open_elective lets the engine recommend a real course instead of an unfillable placeholder. elective_min_level: 200 avoids remedial picks; independent study/special topics/co-op courses are already excluded engine-wide by _pick_open_elective's own name-based filter. ASTRO/GEOSC excluded so 'Supporting Courses and Related Areas' adds real breadth outside the major's own two core departments (same 'outside the major' convention as CMPSC/PHYS's own Supporting Course slots) instead of just recommending more core ASTRO coursework the student would take anyway -- an earlier version of this fix without the exclusion surfaced exactly that (ASTRO 291/292 auto-picked here despite ASTRO 292 already being the correct pick for one of the dedicated Advanced Elective pool items above). Credits bumped from 9 to the bulletin's real 11-credit total (one slot raised from 3 to 5), same convention used for MICRB Elective List C's identical shortfall.
